1. Purpose of Amendment
This amendment provides clarification regarding:
Use of an SBA-certified SDVOSB subcontractor for specialized shredding and document-destruction services;
Licensing and insurance requirements applicable to the prime contractor and subcontractors;
Limitations on subcontracting performance requirements; and
Required container quantities and sizes at each performance location.
Except as specifically amended or clarified herein, all other terms and conditions of the solicitation remain unchanged.

2. Use of an SBA-Certified SDVOSB Subcontractor
Question
May an SBA-certified SDVOSB prime contractor subcontract the physical shredding and document-destruction services to another SBA-certified SDVOSB, provided the arrangement complies with VAAR 852.219-75, 13 CFR 125.6, and the prime contractor retains responsibility for contract performance?
Government Response
Generally, yes. An SBA-certified SDVOSB prime contractor may subcontract work to another properly certified SDVOSB, including substantial physical shredding and document-destruction work, provided the arrangement complies with all applicable requirements, including VAAR 852.219-75 and 13 CFR 125.6.
The prime contractor shall:
Verify that the proposed subcontractor is properly certified as an SDVOSB and qualifies as a similarly situated entity when applicable;
Ensure that the subcontractor performs the work directly and does not further subcontract the work in a manner inconsistent with applicable law or regulation;
Comply with the applicable limitations on subcontracting;
Retain overall responsibility for contract performance, quality control, contract administration, customer communication, security compliance, and required reporting;
Fully disclose the proposed subcontracting arrangement in its quotation; and
Ensure that the subcontracting arrangement is consistent with the technical quotation, price quotation, staffing plan, equipment plan, licensing documentation, and insurance documentation.
Payments to a qualifying similarly situated entity may be treated in accordance with applicable SBA regulations and VAAR requirements when calculating compliance with the limitations on subcontracting. The prime contractor remains responsible for maintaining adequate records demonstrating compliance.
The separately completed and signed VAAR 852.219-75(d) certification is required. The subcontracting approach does not replace the required certification.

3. Licensing and Insurance Requirements
Question
The solicitation requires licensing and insurance documentation in the prime contractor s name. Please clarify the specific licenses and insurance coverages that the prime contractor must independently maintain when specialized shredding services are performed by a qualified subcontractor.
Government Response
The prime contractor shall independently maintain and provide all licenses, registrations, permits, and insurance required by the solicitation, the resulting contract, and applicable federal, state, county, and municipal law for the work for which the prime contractor is responsible.
The prime contractor shall not rely solely on a subcontractor s licenses or insurance to satisfy a requirement expressly imposed on the prime contractor.
As applicable, the prime contractor shall maintain and provide documentation for:
Current business and contractor registrations required in the jurisdictions where services are performed;
Any licenses, registrations, permits, or authorizations required by applicable federal, state, or local law for the services the contractor elects to perform;

Any waste, recycling, transportation, disposal, or related permits applicable to the prime contractor s responsibilities;
Commercial general liability insurance;
Automobile liability insurance for vehicles used in contract performance;
Workers  compensation and employer s liability coverage as required by law; and
Any additional insurance expressly required by the solicitation or resulting contract.
The exact coverage limits, endorsements, certificate wording, effective dates, and additional-insured requirements shall be governed by the solicitation and resulting contract.
The prime contractor shall submit certificates of insurance in the prime contractor s legal name and shall identify the Department of Veterans Affairs or the United States Government as an additional insured when required by the contract.
A subcontractor performing specialized shredding or document-destruction services shall independently maintain all licenses, permits, registrations, and insurance legally required for the work it performs. The prime contractor shall obtain and retain current copies of the subcontractor s documentation and shall verify that the documentation remains current throughout contract performance.
Subcontractor licenses and insurance do not relieve the prime contractor of its contractual responsibilities or of any insurance requirement imposed directly on the prime contractor.
